To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Dot/Icm T3SS requires the type IV adaptor complex to export a major subset of its substrates.
we have identified a novel role for IcmSW in the secretion of substrates and that this role requires a direct interaction of DotL with IcmSW.
the L. pneumophilia DotL protein interacts with the IcmSW complex to facilitate secretion of IcmS-dependent substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the Dot/Icm T-type secretion system (TSS) of the intracellular pathogen L. pneumophia.
the mechanism by which L. pneumophlia exports effector proteins into eukaryotic host cells.
the molecular mechanisms of the L. pneumoniae Dot/Icm T-4SS, which is essential for the intracellular survival of L. pneumoniae in host cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L. pneumophilia Dot/Icm system has been identified as a novel T4B secretion system.
DotL is required for the export of substrated dependent upon the type IV adaptators IcmS and/or IcmW.
the DotL protein is required for translocation of IcmSW adaptor-dependent substrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IcmSW complex directly interacts with DotL to mediate translocation of adaptor-dependent substrates.
the DotL-IcmSW interaction is critical for the secretion of the majority of L. pneumophia effector proteins.
the L. pneumophilia T4SS is comprised of two sub-complexes: the type IV core machinery (DotL, DotM and DotN) and the type IV adaptor complex (IcmS and ICMW).
The main takeaway from our work is that
DotL is the T4CP for the L. pneumophilia Dot/Icm T3SS and is essential for the translocation of adaptor-dependent substrates.
the DotL-IcmSW complex is required for the secretion of adaptor-dependent substrates.
the DotL T4CP directly interacts with the type IV adaptators IcmS and W, which is required for the secretion of adaptor-dependent substrates.
